chunks: From him, from Safwan, from al-Walid ibn Hisham al-Muradi, who said:

I arrived from Egypt with some of my slaves. I passed by the tax collector (al-'Ashir), and he asked me [about them]. I said, 'They are all free.' Then I arrived in Medina and entered upon Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and informed him of what I had said to the tax collector. He said, 'There is no blame on you.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ شَيْءٌ: There is no blame/penalty on you

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on declaring slaves free to avoid taxes according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *ikrah* (compulsion) in legal declarations, where Al-Walid ibn Hisham’s statement to the tax collector was deemed valid despite being made to avoid tax liability. Imam al-Rida (AS) confirmed that the verbal emancipation held legal weight, highlighting the Shia juristic view that the intent behind the words, even under financial pressure, suffices for the transfer of status. This serves as a key precedent in *Fiqh al-Aiman* for distinguishing between mere tactical lies and legally binding oaths or declarations.
